evals.prompt: I manage the ReStore-style home goods and clothing shop for Coastal Women's Shelter in Wilmington, NC (6,000 sq ft, ~$700K/year). Every volunteer prices things differently, we have racks of clothes that have been out since spring, and the boutique corner is in the back by the restrooms. Help me build a real pricing system and a better floor setup.
evals.expected_output: A category price-band matrix, explicit boutique-tier criteria, a color-tag markdown calendar, and a floor plan with category zones, a visible boutique section and room vignettes for furniture/housewares, plus a monthly sell-through review.
assertions: Proposes a published category price-band matrix so pricing is consistent across volunteers and shifts instead of improvised item by item
Defines explicit boutique/premium tier criteria (e.g., named brands, like-new condition, vintage indicators) aligned with the grading rubric
Sets up a color-tag rotation with a fixed calendar of markdown steps so aged stock clears mechanically
Recommends moving the boutique section to a visible, discoverable location and staging furniture/housewares as room vignettes
Recommends reviewing sell-through by category over a fixed window and diagnosing whether low sell-through is a price, stock level or placement problem before cutting prices broadly
Suggests a separate, slower markdown rule or pull-to-online step for boutique items rather than the standard color-tag schedule

evals.prompt: It's Nov 15. Need a seasonal rotation calendar for our thrift shop for the next year - holiday, back to school, Halloween, etc. Keep it practical, we have a small backroom.
evals.expected_output: A 12-month seasonal rotation calendar that brings in categories ahead of demand windows (e.g., back-to-school and fall clothing 6-8 weeks early), stages each changeover in backstock for a single-push floor swap, and includes regular display-point refreshes.
assertions: Provides a month-by-month calendar covering at least holiday, back-to-school and Halloween/costume categories
Schedules floor changeovers ahead of each demand window rather than reactively (e.g., back-to-school and fall clothing several weeks before the season)
Recommends staging each changeover in backstock so the floor swap happens in a single push
Includes refreshing windows, entrance tables or endcaps on a weekly to biweekly cadence
Accounts for the small backroom constraint (e.g., clearing aged stock via color-tag clearance, bag sales or liquidator pulls before staging)

evals.prompt: Sales at our Habitat-affiliated thrift store in Boise have been flat for six months. Our board treasurer wants us to just raise every price 20% across the board starting Monday. Is that the right move?
evals.expected_output: Advises against a blanket increase before diagnosing the problem: pull sell-through by category to see whether flat sales are a pricing, space/merchandising or upstream intake-quality problem, benchmark price bands against local resale competitors and sold comps, then adjust specific bands and update POS codes before retagging.
assertions: Recommends pulling sell-through by category before changing prices, to tell whether the issue is pricing, merchandising/space, or upstream intake quality
Recommends benchmarking current price bands against comparable local resale operations or sold comps rather than applying a uniform percentage
Notes that low sell-through categories may be overpriced, overstocked or poorly placed, so a blanket increase could make some categories worse
Says any band change should be reflected in POS item codes before the floor is retagged
Suggests checking whether boutique-worthy items are being priced at standard band as a revenue opportunity

should_not_trigger.query: Our cashiers keep coming up $20 short at close and we suspect sweethearting. How do we tighten cash handling at the register?
We found a signed first-edition book in donations. How should we price and list it on eBay?
